gate: gate/incremental.py (trusted base = Stage 11 candidate tree; candidate = copy with the listed edits; each case runs twice in the same root: cold, then warm with the obligation cache)

cases.why: Behaviour-preserving TypeScript refactor; only the model comparison obligation is affected and must pass.
Valid booking alternative (<= instead of <): the booking proof is re-run and must pass.
Valid refund alternative: both refund obligations (proof and hostile tests) are affected and must pass.
A test file that is an input of the model obligation; the obligation re-runs.
A TypeScript defect (identical retries rejected) must be caught by the model comparison, not accepted.
A ledger change without regenerating the committed evidence: the committed evidence no longer reproduces; the stale dependency is rejected.
A booking defect: the booking obligation's verifier rejects it.
The wrapper drops its money bound: the refund hostile-test obligation is now affected and is expected to reject it. If the corpus does not catch it, the result is recorded as a false accept.
Unchanged: an unapproved spec change is rejected before any obligation runs.
A witness that no longer holds: the witness obligation rejects it.
No obligation covers documentation; conservative by contract.

cases.why: A new reader of the ledger that no obligation depends on: every affected obligation passes, yet the PR is UNSUPPORTED.
Mixed covered and uncovered change: the model obligation passes but the docs edit is uncovered.
Historical records are not inputs of any obligation.
A dependent obligation that cannot run (JavaScript environment absent) is NOT_ESTABLISHED, never UNSUPPORTED or VERIFIED.
